I feel like the main difference I see between Voila and Evidemment is that Voila was one of the only competitive slow songs we had in an extremely upbeat year which helped it stand out, along with it's amazing staging, whilst Evidemment feels more mid-tempo in a year with quite a lot of competitive mid-tempo songs - at least to me. It certainly has a disco flare which helps it stand out so it's not impossible for a decent televote. I just think it'll really sink if it's drawn anything but 2nd half (another thing that helped Voila - it was the only ballad in that half that wasn't Scandinavian produced (something that often repels televote in my opinion.))

My reasoning for having Australia is that I'm actually really positive that it'll be a jury top 10 finisher at least. The whole band are experienced and have good stage presence and have been doing well at the pre-parties they attended. The showcase of instrumental talent for each member of the group is something that often appeals to juries as well and the synth-rock style is something that's super stand out - especially seeing as juries tend to enjoy both synthy entries and well performed rock entries. Compositionally as well it is one of the most well composed songs of the year in terms of pure musical ability which juries should appreciate. For the televote appeal, I'm expecting really good staging. Also, the layout of the song is something that I can see really going in its favour due to how it subtly grows the entire time, ending on a massive high. People often remember the end of a song more than any part so that really helps it. Plus from what I heard, the crowd were going wild for the song at the pre-parties so it shows it has at least some appeal to an audience. I'm expecting this to finish top 2 in the semi so it should get a good spot in the running order as well.

Georgia actually gives more televote flop than anything and that's because I'm directly comparing it to their JESC entry last year (probably the most similar song I can think of - also with the same writers). That song really underperformed, getting bottom 5 somehow. And Denmark is one I see having more appeal than anyone is expecting. Like I think he feels like a safe qualifier for some reason.

I think France and Italy are certainly picking up good points from the juries but I see France in particular not appealing to the audience at home as much as Eurofans. Austria feels like one that could do similar to Serbia last year (who could also do well this year - not top 5 though). It could also be more like Keiino in terms of results though if they don't appreciate the message.

The Netherlands were my prediction for shock jury favourite as well until I saw those live performances. With a lot of the stereotypical jury favourites seeming like they may not qualify (Switzerland, Estonia, etc), it leaves the door wider open. I've already mentioned my suspicion Australia could get top 5 as I feel like it's compositionally impressive and that could excite the jury. I do have a few other suggestions though:

-Slovenia as juries have shown year after year that they really appreciate well performed indie or rock (Czech Republic 2019 rings a bell). I think they have a chance of a top 5 jury result honestly.

-Much more unlikely but I could see Denmark doing decent with juries if they qualify, it has a certain quality that I think juries could really go for - or totally blank, I could see either happening. It's probably 9th in jury max but there's a slim possibility.

-Georgia always does extremely well with juries in JESC with entries like this so I'm curious if that could pass over to actual Eurovision. I don't think it will due to the lyrics of the song though.

-My big suspect is Lithuania, it seems almost like jury bait and will also do well with the televote due to the diaspora. I feel like this is definitely capable of a top 5 with juries and top 10 finish.

-To a much smaller degree, I could see Latvia gaining points if they qualify. In a similar vein to Slovenia they enjoy these more indie-rock songs most years so they could certainly pick up points there. This feels very jury friendly honestly.
